title: National plans, regional voices: cohesion policy in the next European Union budget
summary_en: The European Commission's 2028–2034 budget proposes consolidating cohesion, agriculture and other funds into integrated National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs). Darvas and co-authors call the integration conceptually sound but identify five required modifications: stronger European-Parliament approval rights, narrower reform-conditionality, policy-specific rules (no agriculture conditions blocking cohesion), independent target-and-result evaluation, and minimum thresholds for cross-border-benefit projects.
policy_relevance: Directly relevant for Hungarian EU-funds strategy (Miniszterelnökség EU Funds department, regional development authorities) and for the Hungarian negotiating position on the next MFF. Hungary as a major net recipient of cohesion funds has strong stakes in (a) keeping conditionality narrow and policy-specific, (b) safeguarding regional-level voice within NRPPs, and (c) protecting cross-border-benefit project envelopes that fund Hungarian connectivity / energy-grid projects.
